articles.title: Supreme Court dismisses Karnataka's review plea against judgment on tribunal to resolve Pennar river dispute
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed Karnataka's review plea against a previous judgment that established a tribunal to resolve the Pennar river water dispute between Karnataka and other states. The tribunal was formed to adjudicate interstate water-sharing issues, and the Supreme Court's decision reinforces the legal framework for resolving such disputes. The ruling impacts water resource management policies between Karnataka and neighboring states.

articles.title: Art. 226 | High Courts Cannot Reweigh Evidence Or Interfere With Factual Findings In Certiorari Jurisdiction : Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has held that the Writ of Certiorari cannot be issued by the High Court to review or reweigh the evidence based on which subordinate courts decided a matter. The Court reiterated that such a jurisdiction is issued only to correct errors of jurisdiction committed by Courts or Tribunals, but not for reappreciation of evidence or acting as a Court of appeal. Holding so, a bench of Justice Sanjay Karol and Justice Vipul M. Pancholi set aside the Karnataka High Court's judgment pass

articles.title: SC questions two-child norm for local polls. 23 yrs ago, it had upheld this rule in landmark verdict
articles.summary: The Supreme Court questioned the constitutional validity of Maharashtra's two-child policy for panchayat elections, which requires candidates to have no more than two children. The revised index, with 2022–23 as the base year, will be released on July 20. This move is part of efforts to track and prioritize key industrial inputs for economic planning.
articles.raw_summary: The government has added iron ore to the list of core infrastructure industries, expanding the Index of Core Industries to nine sectors from eight. The revised series, with 2022–23 as the base year, will be released on July 20.

articles.title: India's forex reserves climb $964 million to $675.16 billion
articles.summary: The RBI said the country's foreign exchange reserves increased by $964 million in the week ended July 10, led by a rise in foreign currency assets. Gold holdings, Special Drawing Rights and India's reserve position with the IMF also edged higher.

articles.title: From AI to guaranteed income: Edelweiss Life lists 5 trends shaping insurance sector
articles.summary: Edelweiss Life, an Indian life insurance company, has identified five trends expected to shape the insurance sector, including regulatory reforms, AI adoption, product innovation, and changing customer preferences. The company suggests these factors will drive the next phase of growth for the industry. The trends highlight the sector's evolving landscape amid technological advancements and regulatory changes.

articles.title: ITC Foods sees El Niño as next big risk for rural demand and food supplies
articles.summary: ITC Foods Divisional CEO Hemant Malik says current demand remains resilient, but a weak monsoon could disrupt agricultural supplies later this year. He also says India must move beyond commodity exports and build global food brands.

articles.title: RVNL partners with Goa government to develop infrastructure projects in the state
articles.summary: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), a state-run company, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Goa government to act as the project execution agency for infrastructure development in the state. While the value, scope, and timelines of the projects are yet to be announced, this collaboration highlights the government's focus on infrastructure expansion. The MoU signifies a formal agreement between the central and state governments to drive development projects.
articles.raw_summary: The state-run company will act as the project execution agency under the MoU, though details on project value, scope and timelines are yet to be announced.

articles.title: IRDAI likely to allow Prudential to retain ICICI Prudential life stake: Sources
articles.summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is likely to allow Prudential Plc to retain its full stake in ICICI Prudential Life after declassification. Sources indicate that the final approval for this decision is expected by late 2026. This move could impact the ownership structure and regulatory compliance of one of India's leading private life insurers.
articles.raw_summary: IRDAI may let Prudential Plc keep its full stake in ICICI Prudential Life after declassification, sources say. Final approval expected by late 2026.

articles.title: Census 2027: Tamil Nadu residents can now fill Census details on this portal
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has launched the Self Enumeration Portal (SEP) for Census 2027, allowing residents to submit their details online starting July 17. This initiative aims to simplify and expedite the census process for locals. The portal is part of the state's administrative efforts to modernize data collection for the upcoming census.
articles.raw_summary: The Self Enumeration Portal (SEP) opens today, July 17, which provides the locals an easier and faster way to submit their information.

articles.title: RBI to roll out digital fraud liability framework from Jan 2027; compensation up to ₹25,000
articles.summary: RBI to launch limited liability framework for digital banking frauds from Jan 1, 2027. Victims get up to ₹25,000 compensation. Governor Sanjay Malhotra announced the move to boost customer protection.

articles.title: Should AI companies be allowed to write the rules that govern them?
articles.summary: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis has called for governments to establish an AI watchdog to regulate the industry. Critics argue that allowing AI companies to shape regulations could concentrate power among major industry players. The debate raises questions about who should govern AI development and its societal impact.
articles.raw_summary: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis wants governments to create an AI watchdog, but critics argue letting AI companies shape future regulations could give the industry's biggest players even more power.

articles.title: Karnataka to roll out comprehensive data centre policy to support infra requirements of AI
articles.summary: Karnataka's government, represented by Atheeq (financial advisor to Chief Minister D K Shivakumar), announced a new comprehensive data centre policy at the GCC Summit 2026. The policy aims to support the infrastructure requirements of artificial intelligence (AI) in the state. The announcement was made in partnership with the Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, and the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission.
articles.raw_summary: Atheeq, who is also the financial advisor to Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, made the announcement at the inaugural edition of the GCC Summit 2026, organised by Maxpo Exhibitions Pvt Ltd. in partnership with the Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, and the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission, here.

articles.title: SC flags 'frustration' of students in CBSE’s digital marking system, seeks SG’s assistance
articles.summary: The Supreme Court expressed concern over students' frustration with CBSE's digital marking system and sought the assistance of Solicitor General Tushar Mehta in a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) that demands the Centre and CBSE frame regulations for conducting exams through the onscreen marking (OSM) system. The court highlighted the need for a structured approach to address the issue, indicating potential policy or regulatory changes in the education sector's digital assessment processes.
articles.raw_summary: Expressing concern over students’ “frustration" in CBSE’s digital marking system, the Supreme Court on Wednesday sought the assistance of Solicitor General Tushar Mehta in hearing a PIL which sought directions to the Centre and the CBSE to frame regulations to conduct exams through onscreen marking (OSM) system.

articles.title: Google required to open up to AI, search engine rivals under EU-mandated changes
articles.summary: The European Commission has mandated that Google must comply with new rules under the Digital Markets Act, requiring the company to open its platform to AI and search engine rivals. This decision follows a six-month review process by the regulator to ensure Google adheres to competition rules. The move impacts Google's operations globally, including in India, where it is a dominant player in the search engine market.
articles.raw_summary: The move by the European Commission, which acts as the EU competition enforcer, came six months after the regulator opened so-called specification proceedings to assist ​the world's most popular internet search engine to comply with the Digital Markets ​Act.
